title: gulf bourses slip iran us escalation dents risk appetite 2026 08 31
text:
BENGALURU, Aug 31 (Reuters) - The Dubai stock market led Gulf stocks lower on Monday as renewed military action between the U.S. and ​Iran near the Strait of Hormuz weighed on risk appetite.
American forces struck two Iranian ‌launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, prompting Tehran to retaliate with attacks on U.S. forces stationed in Jordan. Iran also said it struck a tanker transiting through the strategic waterway.
The United Arab Emirates ​said its air force engaged a drone over its territorial waters that had originated from ​Iran, according to a defence ministry statement on Monday.
Dubai's main index (.DFMGI)
, opens new tab
 fell 0.8%, ⁠with most constituents trading lower. Emirates NBD Bank (ENBD.DU)
, opens new tab
, the emirate's largest lender, dropped 2.3%, while ​developer Emaar Properties (EMAR.DU)
, opens new tab
 declined 1.8%.
Abu Dhabi's benchmark (.FTFADGI)
, opens new tab
 lost 0.4%, pressured by a 3.3% fall in Abu Dhabi ​Islamic Bank (ADIB.AD)
, opens new tab
 and a 1.7% decline in Aldar Properties (ALDAR.AD)
, opens new tab
. Conglomerate Alpha Dhabi Holding (ALPHADHABI.AD)
, opens new tab
 shed 1.2%.
Earlier on Monday, Alpha Dhabi said it doubled its commitment to $1 billion for its private-credit joint venture with Abu Dhabi wealth fund Mubadala Investment.
Qatar's ​benchmark (.QSI)
, opens new tab
 slipped 0.6%, with most sectors in negative territory. Qatar Fuel Company (QFLS.QA)
, opens new tab
 fell 6.7%, while ​Qatar National Bank (QNBK.QA)
, opens new tab
, the region's largest lender, lost 0.6%.
Elsewhere, Qatar's economy shrank 7% in the first quarter of 2026 ‌from ⁠a year earlier, dragged down by a sharp decline in energy production caused by the ongoing Middle East conflict, official data showed.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI)
, opens new tab
 was down 0.3% as real estate and information technology led the broad-based declines. Developer Umm Al Qura for Development (4325.SE)
, opens new tab
 fell 4.9%, while Arabian Internet ​and Communications Services (7202.SE)
, opens new tab
 declined 3.7%.
"Looking ​ahead, sentiment could ⁠lean toward caution as investors monitor any potential escalations and shipping conditions in the Strait of Hormuz," said George Pavel, general manager at Naga.com ​Middle East.
"Stock markets in the region could come under pressure if tensions ​between the ⁠U.S. and Iran deteriorate further. New incidents could overshadow current diplomatic efforts," he added.
Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30)
, opens new tab
 eased 0.1%, pressured by finance, healthcare and communications stocks. Commercial International Bank (COMI.CA)
, opens new tab
 fell 1.3%, while ⁠E-finance (EFIH.CA)
, opens new tab
 slipped 1.9%.
($1 = 3.7544 riyals)
